seasonRead.headline: 2016–17: High-touch offense needs a stabilizer
paragraphs: High-Touch Risk/Reward Scorer is the season’s majority identity, with transition shot volume and failed plays rising together. That is what offensive burden often looks like in a box score: more creation attempts also mean more ways a possession can end.

High-Volume Playmaking Scorer adds higher-quality playmaking, while Two-Way Skill Scorer brings takeaways and assists into the scoring mix. The roster logic is clear—surround the high-touch driver with players who can extend or repair the play.

seasonRead.headline: 2016–17: Several routes to the next possession coexist
paragraphs: Defensive Role Defenseman and Puck-Pressure Transition Defenseman sit almost level, but the useful distinction is not simply safety versus aggression. Both labels contain active puck involvement, and the broad names should not be mistaken for two rigid systems.

Offensive Puck-Moving Defenseman adds a clearer production-and-distribution lane. The hockey read is a plural blue line: different defenders influence the next possession through individual chance creation, recovery pressure or puck movement.
